newsitem.title: USA: NYC mayor opposes dividing economic agency - paper.
newsitem.headline: NYC mayor opposes dividing economic agency - paper.

text.p: New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani opposes a bill that was approved by the state legislature in July that would give the five boroughs more control of economic development, New York Times said.

While the citywide Industrial Development Agency would continue to operate, the new legislation would set up separate agencies for each of the boroughs in an effort to help ensure they each receive their fair share of business incentives.

The paper said aides to Giuliani believed boroughs should not parcel out incentives, like tax cuts, which are designed to attract companies to their areas, as they are not obliged to deal with the impact such breaks have on the city's budget.

Gov. George Pataki has not decided whether he supports the bill, which would oblige the city industrial agency to split 25 percent of its bonding authority among the five boroughs, the paper said. Last year, that percentage would have been about $30 million.
